assumptions.name: Water production cost
assumptions.basis: Illustrative marginal treatment and delivery cost, not a verified Egyptian tariff. Verify against the utility's water production cost ledger and supply contract.

assumptions.name: Service accounts, zone-gov
assumptions.basis: Planning service-account count scaled to the district demand in ZONE_BASE; residential accounts are households, institutional accounts are service connections, not people. Verify against the district occupancy and utility connection registers.

assumptions.name: Utility outage administration, government
assumptions.basis: Illustrative government account-hour budget for notification and utility customer support only; excludes customer economic harm covered by VoLL. Verify against the utility support cost ledger and outage notification work orders.

assumptions.name: Electricity tariff
assumptions.basis: Illustrative purchased-energy rate; Egyptian tariffs cannot be verified offline. Verify against the current electricity supply contract and invoices.

assumptions.name: Crew call-out cost
assumptions.basis: Budget allowance for transport and emergency labour per dispatch. Verify against crew timesheets and the maintenance contractor rate card.

assumptions.name: Pipe repair parts
assumptions.basis: Budget for one district-main joint/section repair. Verify against the pipe bill of quantities and recent supplier quotations.

assumptions.name: Deferred response horizon, pipe_burst
assumptions.basis: Continuing erosion can enlarge excavation and pipe damage; this horizon is a planning scenario. Verify against fault-specific restoration logs and the response SLA.

assumptions.name: Crew response time when sent now
assumptions.basis: One hour is a district dispatch-to-isolation planning allowance. Verify against dispatch logs and the emergency response SLA.

assumptions.name: Late repair multiplier, pipe_burst
assumptions.basis: Continuing erosion can enlarge excavation and pipe damage; the multiplier is a planning allowance, not an estimated growth law. Verify against matched early and deferred repair work orders.

assumptions.name: Maximum deferred repair multiplier
assumptions.basis: Linear escalation m(w) = min(cap, 1 + (late_multiplier_kind - 1) * w / delay_hours_kind) is a planning choice, with a default cap of three times repair cost. Waiting includes losses to w with no additional response hours. This is not a fitted damage-growth law; verify against matched early and deferred repair work orders.

assumptions.name: Ongoing loss cut after pipe isolation
assumptions.basis: Planning allowance: isolation cuts lost-water cost only by 85% after crew arrival until the existing deferred horizon; disruption and secondary purchases continue unchanged. Repair uses planned_factor without damage escalation, plus one extra isolation call-out. Verify against valve isolation plans, post-isolation flows and planned work orders.

assumptions.name: Planned repair cost relative to an emergency repair
assumptions.basis: Planned work is budgeted at 60% of emergency crew-plus-parts cost. Verify against matched planned and emergency maintenance work orders.

assumptions.name: Plausible saving min, pipe_burst
assumptions.basis: Planning review threshold for a single district incident, not a cap on the computed value. Verify against the asset replacement budget and historical incident-loss register.

assumptions.name: Plausible saving max, pipe_burst
assumptions.basis: Planning review threshold for a single district incident, not a cap on the computed value. Verify against the asset replacement budget and historical incident-loss register.
